units.function: Focused HTTP authorization suite preventing Agent callers from storing host-executed workspace provision or teardown commands through Issue create/update APIs.
units.dependencyDirection: Mounts the real Issue route over mocked application services; request actor and nested workspace settings flow inward to a route-level guard before Issue persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Agent JWT/key actor, Issue create input, executionWorkspaceSettings.workspaceStrategy.runtimeProvisionCommand and assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig.workspaceStrategy.teardownCommand.
units.lifecycle: An Agent submits Issue create or patch input containing a host command; the route returns 403 before calling Issue create/update.
units.testAssessment: Two focused cases pass outside the sandbox and prove the guarded create and patch shapes are rejected before persistence. They do not test all command-bearing aliases/nesting, parser bypasses, board-user role/approval matrices, Connector execution, workspace path/environment isolation, secret/data egress, concurrency or stable machine-readable errors. Nearly all access services are permissive mocks.
units.designRationale: Close a direct privilege-escalation path where an untrusted Agent could turn control-plane fields into arbitrary host commands.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must prevent an Agent or compromised Connector from manufacturing host execution authority through task/workspace metadata, while allowing accountable humans to request controlled environment setup.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the early reject-before-persistence invariant and maintain adversarial tests. Do not expose free-form host shell commands as a normal Company OS core field: use typed WorkspaceProvisionPlan references, policy-evaluated capabilities, accountable-human approval for elevated actions, a local execution-node boundary, signed digests, strict path/env/secret/data-egress controls, lease fencing and durable execution receipts. Return stable errorCode plus parameters.
units.responsibilityConflict: The guard distinguishes Agent from non-Agent but does not establish which human is authorized and accountable for dangerous commands. A free-form command retained as product data can bypass approval, move secrets or data, and create ambiguous responsibility when later executed by a Connector.
evidence: git history: eleven commits from dcac49a4fd4739ec7177b196a869aa5d1cc169d9 through 73eb23734f25c570d88665e672f80d740797c632 recorded in the read ledger
2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 2/2 failed on TCP EPERM only
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL threat correctly recognized: Agent-controlled runtimeProvisionCommand/teardownCommand would be host RCE. POSITIVE: both tested paths fail before persistence. CRITICAL residual design risk for Company OS: free-form host commands need typed plans, execution-node isolation, approval and digest binding rather than actor-type filtering alone. HIGH coverage gap: only two shapes are tested and access is otherwise mocked allow. HIGH governance gap: no human role/accountability or high-risk approval test. HIGH egress gap: path, environment, secret and outbound-data controls are not demonstrated. MEDIUM contract gap: assertion depends on English error prose rather than a stable code.
